strings.d1.s0.name: Sky Tower
strings.d1.s0.tips: At 328 m, the tallest tower in the Southern Hemisphere. Glass floor; SkyWalk and SkyJump cost extra. Book online.
strings.d1.s1.name: Auckland Art Gallery
strings.d1.s1.tips: Māori and Pacific art under a kauri timber roof. Free entry (20 NZD for foreign visitors).
strings.d1.s2.name: Albert Park & Üniversite
strings.d1.s2.tips: Victorian park with a floral clock.
strings.d1.s3.name: Depot Eatery Federal Street
strings.d1.s3.tips: Al Brown's oyster and seafood bar, right below the Sky Tower.
strings.d1.s4.name: Viaduct Harbour & Wynyard Quarter
strings.d1.s4.tips: Marina with America's Cup yachts. Visit Silo Park and the Maritime Museum (25 NZD).
strings.d1.b0.name: Auckland Fish Market Wynyard
strings.d1.b0.tips: Fish market food hall: try the fish and chips.
strings.d1.b1.name: New Zealand Maritime Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: From Polynesian canoes to yachts, plus a boat tour of the harbour.
strings.d2.s0.name: Waiheke Ferry Fullers
strings.d2.s0.tips: 40 minutes from Downtown (return about 60 NZD) across the Hauraki Gulf.
strings.d2.s1.name: Oneroa Beach & Village
strings.d2.s2.name: Mudbrick Vineyard
strings.d2.s2.tips: Vineyard and restaurant with city views. Try the syrah; book ahead.
strings.d2.s3.name: Cable Bay Vineyards
strings.d2.s3.tips: Neighbouring vineyard with wine and cheese platters on the terrace.
strings.d2.s4.name: Onetangi Beach
strings.d2.s4.tips: Winter beach walk. Stonyridge vineyard (Larose) is an alternative.
strings.d2.b0.name: Man O' War Vineyard
strings.d2.b0.tips: Beachfront vineyard at the far end of the island. Take a taxi or drive.
strings.d2.b1.name: Waiheke EcoZip
strings.d2.b1.tips: Zipline with forest and sea views; an alternative to wine tasting.
strings.d3.s0.name: Mount Eden
strings.d3.s0.tips: 196 m volcanic crater with 360° views of the city and Sky Tower. Best in morning light.
strings.d3.s1.name: Auckland War Memorial Museum
strings.d3.s1.tips: Māori hall (war canoe, marae), haka performance (extra) and volcano gallery, set in the Domain park.
strings.d3.s2.name: Devonport Ferry
strings.d3.s3.name: Mount Victoria Devonport
strings.d3.s3.tips: Short climb to views of the city skyline and Rangitoto opposite. Winter guns are in place.
strings.d3.s4.name: Devonport Chocolates & Waterfront
strings.d3.s4.tips: Town main street, chocolate and Cheltenham Beach.
strings.d3.b0.name: Wintergarden Domain
strings.d3.b0.tips: Glasshouses next to the museum. Free.
strings.d3.b1.name: Devonport Stone Oven Bakery
strings.d4.s0.name: Arataki Visitor Centre
strings.d4.s0.tips: Gateway to the Waitākere forest (45 minutes by car). Māori carvings and views.
strings.d4.s1.name: Kitekite Falls
strings.d4.s1.tips: 40 m waterfall. Easy 1-hour return walk, with a swimming pool at the base.
strings.d4.s2.name: Piha Beach & Lion Rock
strings.d4.s2.tips: Winter waves; beach walk and the rock.
strings.d4.s3.name: Piha Cafe
strings.d4.s3.tips: Beach café with fish and coffee.
strings.d4.s4.name: Karekare Beach
strings.d4.s4.tips: The beach from the film The Piano. Waterfall and empty sands.
strings.d4.b0.name: Muriwai Gannet Colony
strings.d4.b0.tips: Gannet colony (August to March); an alternative to Karekare.
strings.d4.b1.name: Elevation Café Waitakere
strings.d4.b1.tips: Café with views on the Scenic Drive.
strings.d5.s0.name: Hobbiton Movie Set
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2.5 hours to Matamata (tour about 250 NZD from Auckland). 44 hobbit holes, with a beer included at the Green Dragon. Book online weeks ahead.
strings.d5.s1.name: Matamata Lunch
strings.d5.s2.name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
strings.d5.s2.tips: Glowworm cave reached by quiet boat. No photography; Ruakuri costs extra.
strings.d5.s3.name: Waitomo Caves Village
strings.d5.s3.tips: Short break before the 3-hour drive back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ruakuri Cave
strings.d5.b0.tips: Cave with a spiral entrance. Photography allowed; an alternative to Glowworm Caves.
strings.d5.b1.name: Huhu Cafe Waitomo
strings.d5.b1.tips: The best café in the cave town.
strings.d6.s0.name: Rangitoto Island Ferry
strings.d6.s1.name: Rangitoto Summit Track
strings.d6.s1.tips: 1-hour climb of 260 m past lava caves and the crater, through the world's largest pohutukawa forest. Bring water, as there are no shops.
strings.d6.s2.name: Rangitoto Wharf Return
strings.d6.s2.tips: Ferries at 12:45 and 15:30 back to the city.
strings.d6.s3.name: Ponsonby Road
strings.d6.s3.tips: Boutiques and cafés, plus the Ponsonby Central food court.
strings.d6.s4.name: Ponsonby Central
strings.d6.s4.tips: Food market: try Bird on a Wire chicken and El Sizzling Chorizo.
strings.d6.b0.name: Tiritiri Matangi Island
strings.d6.b0.tips: Bird sanctuary island (takahe, kokako). Ferries Wednesday to Sunday; an alternative to Rangitoto.
strings.d6.b1.name: Ponsonby Dizengoff
strings.d7.s0.name: Tamaki Drive Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Coastal road with views of Okahu Bay and Rangitoto.
strings.d7.s1.name: Mission Bay Beach
strings.d7.s1.tips: City beach with a fountain. Kelly Tarlton's aquarium is nearby.
strings.d7.s2.name: Mission Bay Breakfast
strings.d7.s2.tips: Cafés opposite the beach. Eggs benedict for a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Britomart SkyDrive
strings.d7.b0.name: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life
strings.d7.b0.tips: Penguins and a shark tunnel; an alternative to the beach.
strings.d7.b1.name: Giapo Ice Cream
strings.d7.b1.tips: Ice cream as art, on Gore Street.
strings.note0: Use AT HOP or contactless. Ferries are run by Fullers (Waiheke and Rangitoto need separate tickets). The SkyDrive airport bus takes 45 minutes. For Piha and Hobbiton, hire a car or take a tour (drive on the left).
strings.note1: December to February is summer, at 22-26°C, when Waiheke and the beaches are lively. Pohutukawa trees bloom red in December. Christmas falls in midsummer and hotels fill up.
strings.note2: The NZeTA and IVL tourist levy are paid online. Turkish citizens need a visa (check this). Coffee costs 5-6 NZD, a café meal 25 and a tour 250. Tipping is not expected.
strings.note3: Book Hobbiton online weeks ahead. Photography is banned at Waitomo. Rangitoto has no water or shops. At Piha, rip currents can be deadly, so obey the flags.
strings.note4: Māori culture is best seen in the museum, with a haka. 'Kia ora' is a greeting. Try fish and chips, a flat white and hokey pokey ice cream.
strings.note5: UV levels are very high (thin ozone layer). In summer you can burn in 15 minutes.
strings.transit.name: AT HOP / contactless
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers buses, trains and ferries (some, such as Devonport and Waiheke, excepted). Contactless bank cards also work.
